transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?
I don’t enjoy my job or any of the things I used to love doing anymore, and it’s been like this for weeks. I just feel completely flat and nothing seems to interest me lately.
Have you ever had a similar period of feeling depressed or losing interest in things before this episode?

Yes, looking back, this isn't the first time I've felt like this. I've actually noticed these big swings between being really revved-up and then falling into these heavy, low downturns happening off and on for several years now.
During the times when you felt really revved-up, did you need much less sleep than usual, feel unusually energetic or confident, or do things that were out of character or risky?

Yes, I felt incredibly energetic and unusually confident, like I was buzzing with energy and staying up until midnight working on ideas because I truly believed I was the only one who could reinvent our brand. I didn't do anything highly risky or dangerous, but I did take on an overwhelming amount of extra work and projects because I just couldn't slow down.
How long did those 'revved-up' periods usually last—were they at least 4 days, or did they continue for a week or more?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact count, but they definitely lasted for at least a few days or a week during those busy times. It felt like a solid block of time where I was constantly on the go before the energy finally wore off.
During those high-energy periods, did you ever become so elevated or irritable that you needed hospitalization, had very little need for sleep, or had trouble functioning because of your behavior?

No, I never needed to be hospitalized, and my managers actually praised my work and initiative during those times. I did get quite irritable and snapped at my husband and coworkers over tiny things, and I'd stay up until midnight sketching out ideas because I was buzzing with energy. But it didn't cause severe trouble functioning or lead to any hospital stays.
Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week where your mood was so elevated or irritable that it caused major problems at work, with relationships, or led to hospitalization?

I have had periods lasting a week or more where I felt incredibly amped up and easily irritated, but it never led to hospitalization or ruined my career. Even though I was highly distracted and snapped at my husband and coworkers over small things, my managers actually praised my high energy and initiative. It felt overwhelming to me internally, but it didn't cause major external damage.
During those high-energy periods, did you ever have symptoms so severe that you lost touch with reality, needed hospitalization, or caused major problems at work or in your relationships?

No, I never lost touch with reality or needed hospitalization, and my high energy at work was actually praised as initiative, though I did snap at my husband and coworkers occasionally. The major problems, like my performance reviews slipping and backing out of my responsibilities at home, only started recently during this low period.
During your high-energy periods, did you ever hear or see things ուրիշ people couldn’t, or believe things that others said were clearly not true?
No, I have never heard or seen things that weren't actually there. I also haven't held any beliefs that others found completely untrue or unrealistic, even during my high-energy phases.

During your high-energy periods, did you ever have a time when the symptoms were severe enough to cause major problems at work or home, or did they last for a full week or more with marked impairment?

No, those high-energy periods didn't cause any major disruptions or severe impairment, and my managers actually praised my productivity at the time. The real problems, like my performance reviews slipping and withdrawing from my chores and social life, only started happening during these recent low periods.
Have you had a period of feeling depressed or losing interest that lasted at least 2 weeks, most of the day nearly every day?

Yes, this low, flat feeling and total loss of interest has been happening almost every single day. It has actually been dragging on like this for about six months now, ever since my big product relaunch project wrapped up.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week when you felt so unusually energetic or irritable that you needed much less sleep, talked much more than usual, felt your thoughts racing, or did things that were clearly out of character for you?

Yes, I've had periods like that, particularly during a product relaunch over the past year and off and on for several years. I would feel on top of the world and buzz with energy, staying up late to start extra projects and sketches because I couldn't slow down. I also became very irritable during those times and would easily snap at my husband and coworkers over minor things.
During your high-energy periods, did you ever have symptoms so severe that you needed hospitalization, lost touch with reality, or had major problems at work or in your relationships?

No, I never lost touch with reality or needed to be hospitalized, and my managers actually praised my high energy as initiative. I did get very irritable and snapped at my husband and coworkers over minor things, but it didn't cause major disruptions. The real problems, like my performance slipping, only started during this current low period.
When you had those high-energy periods, did they last for at least 4 days in a row, or were they usually shorter than that?

Yes, they lasted much longer than four days. During the product relaunch, that revved-up state went on for weeks or even months at a time. Looking back over the years, those high-energy stretches have always lasted well over a few days at a time.

During those high-energy periods, did you ever feel so unusually energized or irritable that you needed much less sleep, talked much more than usual, or had racing thoughts for at least a full week at a time?

During those periods, which have happened off and on for several years, I definitely felt extremely energized, buzzed, and very easily irritated. However, I don't recall having racing thoughts or talking much more than usual. And while I did work late into the night, I don't specifically remember having a reduced need for sleep.
During those high-energy periods, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual and still had plenty of energy the next day, or were you just staying up late because you were busy?

I'm not quite sure or haven't really thought about whether I actually needed less sleep or if I was just staying up late because I was so busy. But I can definitely confirm that I stayed up very late working on new ideas and felt incredibly buzzed while doing it.
During those high-energy periods, did you actually need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested the next day, or were you just staying up late because you were busy?

I'm not entirely sure if I actually needed less sleep to feel rested, or if I was just staying up late because my mind was racing with all those projects. I just remember being so buzzed with energy that I couldn't seem to wind down at night.
During those high-energy periods, did you actually need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested the next day, or were you just staying up late because you were busy?

To be honest, I'm really not sure if my body actually needed less sleep to function or if I was just pushing through because I was so busy and driven. I just know I was staying up very late working on those ideas and felt too wired to sleep.
During those high-energy periods, did you actually feel rested on much less sleep than usual, or were you just staying up late because you were busy and wired?
I don't recall exactly how my sleep quality was or if I felt rested on less sleep. I just know that I definitely felt incredibly wired, stayed up very late, and had a ton of energy at the time.
Have your high-energy periods ever caused major problems at work, serious relationship conflict, or been severe enough that you needed hospitalization or became unable to function normally?

No, those high-energy times didn't cause major problems or lead to hospitalization, and my managers actually praised my initiative, though I did snap at my husband and coworkers over small things. The real issues, like my work performance slipping and my husband having to pick up the slack, have only happened during this current low period.

Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt clearly more energetic or irritable than usual and also had a noticeably decreased need for sleep, talking more, racing thoughts, or doing more goal-directed activity than normal?

Yes, I've definitely had periods like that lasting well over four days, especially during the product relaunch and off and on for several years. I felt incredibly amped up and irritable, and I took on an overwhelming amount of extra goals and projects because I was buzzing with energy. I'm not really sure about having a decreased need for sleep or racing thoughts, but the high energy and constant activity were definitely there.

Between these high-energy periods, have you ever had at least 2 months when your mood and energy were completely back to normal, or have the ups and downs been happening most of the time for years without long breaks?

Yes, these swings have been happening off and on for several years now. However, I do have periods in between where my mood and energy level out and I feel relatively normal. It isn't a constant, unbroken cycle of ups and downs without breaks.
Have your mood swings happened for at least 2 years, with periods of feeling normal in between, but never a full 2 months completely free of symptoms?

Yes, these big swings between my high and low periods have been happening off and on for several years now, and I definitely have times where I feel normal in between. However, I'm not entirely sure if I've ever gone a full two months completely free of any symptoms during those breaks. It is just hard to remember the exact timeline of how long those normal stretches lasted.
Between these mood swings, have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 months where you felt completely back to normal with no significant depression or high-energy symptoms?

I'm not entirely sure or cannot recall a specific stretch of two months where I felt completely normal. It feels like I've just been bouncing between these highs and lows for a long time without a clear, stable middle ground.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 months where you felt completely back to normal with no significant depression or high-energy symptoms?

I'm really not sure and can't recall a specific, clear two-month stretch of feeling completely normal. It feels like I've just been cycling between these high and low periods for several years without any kind of distinct, prolonged break.

Have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 months where you felt completely back to normal with no significant mood symptoms, or have the ups and downs been present most of the time for at least 2 years?

Yes, these big swings between being highly revved-up and feeling deeply down have been happening off and on for several years now. I do have periods in between where I feel more like myself, but this overall pattern of ups and downs has been present for a very long time.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 months where you felt completely back to normal with no significant depression or high-energy symptoms?

I'm not entirely sure, as it feels like I've been bouncing between these highs and lows for several years now. I can't quite recall a solid two-month stretch where I felt completely normal or balanced.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 months where you felt completely back to normal with no significant depression or high-energy symptoms?

Actually, yes, I do have periods where I feel completely back to my normal self between those high and low swings. These stable, normal periods have occurred off and on over the last several years, lasting for a few months at a time before the cycle of highs and lows starts up again.
Have these mood swings been present for at least 2 years, with many ups and downs but no full 2-month period completely free of symptoms?

Yes, these big swings between my high and low periods have definitely been happening off and on for several years now. As for this current low stretch, it has been dragging on continuously for about six months.
When you had the high-energy periods, did they last at least 4 days in a row, or were they shorter than that?

Yes, they definitely lasted much longer than four days, often going on for weeks or even months at a time, like during the product relaunch. These high-energy cycles, followed by the low periods, have been happening off and on for several years now.
Have there ever been periods lasting 2 years or more where your mood has been up and down most of the time, but you were never symptom-free for more than 2 months at a time?

I'm not quite sure about the exact timing or if I've ever gone more than two months feeling completely normal during those years. It's just hard for me to recall the exact timeline of my mood changes over such a long period.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports bipolar disorder with recurrent hypomanic/manic-spectrum episodes and a current major depressive episode. The patient described multiple past elevated periods lasting at least several days to weeks, with increased energy, inflated confidence, increased goal-directed activity, irritability, and staying up late, but without psychosis or hospitalization. The current episode is a depressive syndrome lasting about 6 months with marked anhedonia and low mood. This pattern is more consistent with bipolar affective disorder than cyclothymia, because the history includes clear syndromal depressive and elevated episodes rather than only chronic subthreshold fluctuations.
